updateTarget.displayName: Build and Test Your First AWS Lambda Function

programme.displayName: Build and Test Your First AWS Lambda Function
programme.subtitle: Create, test, and clean up a simple Node.js Lambda function.
programme.description: Create a small AWS Lambda function in Europe (London), test it with safe sample JSON, review its logs, and remove only the resources created in this Follow Along.
programme.learningOutcome: Create and test a Node.js Lambda function, view its invocation logs, and manually clean up the Lambda resources created for this exercise.

phases.title: Prepare access
phases.description: Create a clearly named IAM user record, then stop for administrator-approved access setup before using that identity.

phases.title: Create and test the function
phases.description: Create a Node.js Lambda function, replace the starter code, and test it with harmless sample input.

phases.title: Observe and clean up
phases.description: Review the invocation evidence in CloudWatch Logs, verify the result, and manually remove only this Follow Along's resources.

tasks.title: Create the IAM User Record
tasks.goal: Create an IAM user named follow-along-lambda-user without creating access keys or entering secret data.
tasks.whyItMatters: IAM users have no permissions by default. Creating the user separately makes the access boundary visible before any Lambda resources are created.

consoleSteps.title: Open IAM
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The IAM dashboard opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Use an existing authorized administrator identity for this step.

consoleSteps.title: Start user creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Create user page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Name the user
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter follow-along-lambda-user as the user name.

instructions.text: Enter follow-along-lambda-user as the user name.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The user name is shown as follow-along-lambda-user.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use a personal name or confidential information.

consoleSteps.title: Avoid credential creation
consoleSteps.instruction: Do not create an access key.

instructions.text: Do not create an access key.
Do not enter passwords or secrets in this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: No access key or secret value is created or recorded by this Follow Along.
consoleSteps.warning: Access keys, passwords, and MFA setup are credentials and are intentionally outside this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Create the user
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Users list includes follow-along-lambda-user.
consoleSteps.warning: The new IAM user has no permissions until an authorized administrator assigns organization-approved access.

cliSteps.explanation: Creates the same IAM user record by using AWS CLI credentials that are already configured outside this Follow Along.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes a User object with UserName follow-along-lambda-user.
cliSteps.warning: This command does not create access keys, a console password, or permissions.

verification.title: Confirm the IAM user record
verification.instruction: In IAM, search Users for follow-along-lambda-user.
verification.expectedResult: The search returns exactly the IAM user created for this Follow Along.

tasks.feature: Lambda function, Node.js runtime, and execution role
tasks.goal: Create follow-along-lambda-area in eu-west-2, replace its starter code, and deploy the update.
tasks.whyItMatters: This introduces a Lambda function, its handler, and the execution role that lets the function write invocation logs.

consoleSteps.title: Open Lambda in the correct Region
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Lambda Functions page is open in eu-west-2.
consoleSteps.warning: Create and later delete the function in the same Region.

consoleSteps.title: Start function creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Basic information section is displayed.

consoleSteps.title: Set function basics
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter follow-along-lambda-area as the function name.

instructions.text: Enter follow-along-lambda-area as the function name.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The function settings show the fixed test name, Node.js 24.x, and x86_64.
consoleSteps.warning: Use the exact function name so the log group is easy to identify during cleanup.

consoleSteps.title: Create the function
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The function page opens for follow-along-lambda-area.
consoleSteps.warning: Lambda creates an execution role for this console workflow that provides basic CloudWatch Logs access.

consoleSteps.title: Open the code file
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The built-in code editor displays index.mjs.

consoleSteps.title: Replace the starter code
consoleSteps.instruction: Replace the starter code with the documented area-calculation example.

instructions.text: Replace the starter code with the documented area-calculation example.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The handler reads length and width, logs the calculated area, and returns an area response.
consoleSteps.warning: Use only the harmless test values in this Follow Along. Do not add passwords, keys, tokens, or personal data.

consoleSteps.title: Deploy the code
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The console confirms that the function code was updated.
consoleSteps.warning: Code changes are not active until deployment succeeds.

cliSteps.explanation: Checks the function created in the console without changing it.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies follow-along-lambda-area and its configuration.
cliSteps.warning: Run this only after the console creation step has completed.

verification.title: Confirm the deployed function

tasks.title: Invoke the Function with a Test Event
tasks.feature: Lambda test event and synchronous invocation
tasks.goal: Run follow-along-lambda-area with length 6 and width 7 and confirm an area of 42.
tasks.whyItMatters: A saved test event shows how Lambda passes JSON input to the Node.js handler and returns the result.

consoleSteps.title: Open the Test tab
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The test-event editor opens.

consoleSteps.title: Name the test event
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter area-test as the event name.

instructions.text: Enter area-test as the event name.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The event is named area-test and is private.
consoleSteps.warning: Private test events are available only to their creator.

consoleSteps.title: Enter safe sample JSON
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter the JSON object with length 6 and width 7.

instructions.text: Enter the JSON object with length 6 and width 7.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The saved event contains the two numeric values.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not put secrets or personal information in a Lambda test event.

consoleSteps.title: Run the test
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Execution result reports Succeeded and returns an area of 42.
consoleSteps.warning: If the result differs, check the code, deploy it again, and rerun the test.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda invoke --function-name follow-along-lambda-area --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --payload '{"length":6,"width":7}' response.json --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Synchronously invokes the deployed function with the same harmless JSON input and writes the function response to response.json.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command response reports StatusCode 200, and response.json contains the function response.
cliSteps.warning: The quoted JSON syntax is for Unix-like shells; adapt quotation marks for your terminal if necessary.

verification.title: Confirm the area result
verification.expectedResult: Status is Succeeded and the response contains an area of 42.

tasks.title: Inspect the Invocation Logs
tasks.goal: Find the successful invocation records for follow-along-lambda-area in its CloudWatch Logs log group.
tasks.whyItMatters: Logs provide evidence that the handler ran and show the request lifecycle records used for basic troubleshooting.

consoleSteps.title: Open the monitoring page
consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudWatch opens the log group for follow-along-lambda-area.
consoleSteps.warning: Logs can take a short time to appear after the first invocation.

consoleSteps.title: Open the newest log stream

instructions.text: Choose the stream with the newest Last event time.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The log stream displays records from the test invocation.

consoleSteps.title: Find the successful invocation records
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The stream shows the calculated area and Lambda invocation lifecycle records.
consoleSteps.warning: Refresh the log-stream list if the newest invocation is not visible yet.

cliSteps.explanation: Lists the function log streams with the newest activity first.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes one or more log streams for the Lambda function after a successful invocation.
cliSteps.warning: Run this after invoking the function at least once.

verification.title: Confirm the invocation log
verification.expectedResult: The stream contains the area calculation and the START, END, and REPORT records.

tasks.title: Clean Up the Follow Along Resources
tasks.feature: Lambda, CloudWatch Logs, and IAM cleanup
tasks.goal: After verifying the function, manually remove only the Lambda function, its log group, its generated execution role, and the IAM user record created for this Follow Along.
tasks.whyItMatters: Cleanup reduces account clutter and prevents unintended ongoing use of the practice resources.

consoleSteps.title: Record the execution role name
consoleSteps.expectedResult: You have the exact role name created for follow-along-lambda-area.
consoleSteps.warning: Record only the role name. Do not copy credentials or secret values.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the Lambda function
consoleSteps.expectedResult: follow-along-lambda-area no longer appears in the Functions list.
consoleSteps.warning: Delete only the function with the exact fixed test name.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the Lambda log group
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the CloudWatch Log groups page.

instructions.text: Open the CloudWatch Log groups page.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The function log group no longer appears in eu-west-2.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the generated execution role

instructions.text: Search for the recorded role name.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The generated execution role no longer appears in IAM.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not delete a shared or unfamiliar role.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the IAM user record
consoleSteps.expectedResult: follow-along-lambda-user no longer appears in IAM.
consoleSteps.warning: Before deletion, an administrator must remove any credentials or permissions that were added outside this Follow Along.

cliSteps.explanation: Deletes only the Lambda function created for this Follow Along.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without returning a function object.
cliSteps.warning: Run only after recording the execution-role name and completing all verification.

cliSteps.explanation: Permanently deletes only the Lambda log group created for this Follow Along.
Deletes the IAM user record created for this Follow Along after all externally added user items have been removed.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output when the user has no remaining attached items.
cliSteps.warning: AWS CLI IAM-user deletion requires attached items to be removed first; do not remove unfamiliar items.

findings.message: The requested update asks for an IAM user with the correct permissions, but no organization-approved permission model or policy ARN was supplied. This package intentionally does not invent, attach, or propose an IAM policy. An authorized administrator must determine and grant the least-privilege permissions required by the organization's controls before follow-along-lambda-user can be used for Lambda work.
The IAM user task creates only a named IAM user record and deliberately creates no access keys, console password, or other credentials. It therefore cannot by itself provide usable Lambda access.

The documented console tutorial creates an execution role automatically for the function with basic CloudWatch Logs access. The exact generated role name is account-specific and must be recorded during cleanup rather than guessed.
